source_text: Ὁδοὶ δύο εἰσί, μία τῆς ζωῆς καὶ μια τοῦ θανάτου, διαφορὰ δὲ πολλὴ μεταξὺ τῶν δύο ὁδῶν. Ἡ μὲν οὖν ὁδὸς τῆς ζωῆς ἐστιν αὕτη: πρῶτον ἀγαπήσεις τὸν θεὸν τὸν ποιήσαντά σε, δεύτερον τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν: πάντα δὲ ὅσα ἐὰν θελήσῃς μὴ γίνεσθαί σοι, καὶ σὺ ἄλλῳ μὴ ποίει. Τούτων δὲ τῶν λόγων ἡ διδαχή ἐστιν αὕτη: εὐλογεῖτε τοῦς καταρωμένους ὑμῖν καὶ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐχθρῶν ὑμῶν, νηστεύετε δὲ ὑπὲρ τῶν διωκόντων ὑμᾶς: ποία γὰρ χάρις, ἐὰν ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς; οὐχὶ καὶ τὰ ἔθνη τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν; ὑμεῖς δὲ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς μισοῦντας ὑμᾶς, καὶ οὐχ ἕξετε ἐχθρόν. ἀπέχου τῶν σαρκικῶν καὶ σωματικῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν: ἐάν τίς σοι δῷ ῥάπισμα εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν σιαγόνα, στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην, καὶ ἔσῃ τέλειος: ἐὰν ἀγγαρεύσῃ σέ τις μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετ’ αὐτοῦ δύο: ἐὰν ἄρῃ τις τὸ ἱμάτιόν σου, δὸς αὐτῷ καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα: ἐὰν λάβῃ τις ἀπὸ σοῦ τὸ σόν, μὴ ἀπαίτει: οὐδὲ γὰρ δύνασαι. παντὶ τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου καὶ μὴ ἀπαίτει: πᾶσι γὰρ θέλει δίδοσθαι ὁ πατὴρ ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων χαρισμάτων. μακάριος ὁ διδοὺς κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν: ἀθῷος γάρ ἐστιν. οὐαὶ τῷ λαμβάνονται: εἰ μὲν γὰρ χρείαν ἔχων λαμβάνει τις, ἀθῷος ἔσται: ὁ δὲ μὴ χρείαν ἔχων δώσει δίκην, ἱνατί ἔλαβε καὶ εἰς τί: ἐν συνοχῇ δὲ γενόμενος ἐξετασθήσεται περὶ ὧν ἔπραξε, καὶ οὐκ ἐξελεύσεται ἐκεῖθεν, μέχρις οὗ ἀποδῷ τὸν ἔσχατον κοδράντην. ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ τούτου δὲ εἴρηται: Ἱδρωσάτω ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη σου εἰς τὰς χεῖράς σου, μέχρις ἂν γνῷς, τίνι δῷς.
pass_a_gloss: There are two ways, one of life and one of death, and there is a great difference between the two ways. The way of life is this: first you will love God who made you, second your neighbor as yourself; and all things which you wish not to happen to you, do not do to another. The teaching of these words is this: bless those who curse you and pray for your enemies, and fast for those who persecute you: for what thankfulness is it, if you love those who love you? Do not even the nations do the same? But you love those who hate you, and you will not have an enemy. Keep away from fleshly and bodily desires: if someone gives you a slap on the right cheek, turn to him also the other, and you will be perfect; if someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two; if someone takes your coat, give him also your shirt; if someone takes what is yours, do not ask for it back: for you are not able. Give to everyone who asks you and do not ask for it back: for the Father wants to give to all from his own gifts. Blessed is the one who gives according to the command: for he is guiltless. Woe to the one who receives: for if someone receives because he has need, he will be guiltless; but the one who has no need and gives will give account, for what reason he received and for what purpose: and being in distress he will be examined concerning what he did, and he will not go out from there until he pays back the last quadrans. But also concerning this it has been said: let your charity sweat in your hands, until you know to whom you give.

pass_b_english: There are two ways — one of life, one of death — and the difference between them is vast. The way of life is this: first, love the God who made you; second, love your neighbor as yourself. And whatever you would not want done to you, do not do to anyone else.

This is the teaching of those words: bless those who curse you and pray for your enemies; fast for those who persecute you. After all, what credit is it if you love only those who love you? Even the nations do that. But you are to love those who hate you, and then you will have no enemy.

Keep clear of fleshly and bodily desires. If someone slaps you on the right cheek, turn the other to him as well, and you will be complete. If anyone forces you to go one mile, go with him two. If someone takes your coat, give him your shirt too. If someone takes what belongs to you, do not demand it back, because you are not able to. Give to everyone who asks you, and do not ask for it back, for the Father wants to give to all from his own gifts.

Blessed is the one who gives according to the command, for he is guiltless. Woe to the one who receives: if someone receives because he is in need, he will be guiltless; but the one who has no need and yet receives will give an account — why he took it and for what purpose. And while he is held in custody, he will be examined concerning what he did, and he will not get out until he has paid back the last quadrans. It has also been said about this: 'Let your charity sweat in your hands until you know to whom you give.' (Matthew 5:39-42; Matthew 6:14-15; Luke 6:27-31)

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Greek text. Pass A provides a faithful literal translation, and Pass B provides a fluent version that correctly identifies the scriptural parallels (Matthew 5:39-42; Matthew 6:14-15; Luke 6:27-31) for the content provided. All clauses, including the conditional statements regarding receiving and the final exhortation on charity, are preserved.
